
# Cellfinder

## Cellfinder

Cellfinder is the BrainGlobe tool for detecting cell coordinates

## Plan

Explore cellfinder in more depth, and more breadth

## Whole brain microscopy

Microscope image

## Cell finder input data

two channels - lightsheet or stpt

## Applications

Viral tracing,
Cfos (experimental)
Maybe others ?

Want to find cell centres.

## What problems is it designed to overcome?

* Classical image processing lacks sweet spot in noisy 3d microscopy. E.g thresholding always includes noise or excludes cells
* ML based methods are slow on such large data

## Cellfinder strategy

Best of both worlds

* Select too many possible cells: "candidates"
* Use machine-learning to classify candidates as cell/not cell
    * needs curation and re-training

## Cellfinder candidate detection (2d filter)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

:::{.incremental}
1. Clip to reserve 2 values
2. Keep tiles with average intensity > avg+2*std(corner tiles) ("TileWalker")
3. Enhance peaks
    a) median filter
    b) gaussian filter
    c) laplacian filter
4. Threshold at plane avg+nds*std
:::

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img/detection.png)
:::
:::

## Cellfinder candidate detection (3d filter+structure splitting)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

:::{.incremental}
1. Looks at sphere (ellipsoid) around each pixel
2. If sufficient pixels in the ellipsoid are bright, mark as candidate
3. Split structure if needed
4. Return centres of structures
:::

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img/detection.png)
:::
:::

## Cellfinder classification

Uses both channels. Assumption:
* noise is bright in both channels
* signal is bright only in one channel

## Curation and retraining

Suggested strategy
* spend hours, not days curating
* iterate fast: curate, retrain, classify and repeat
* curated balanced data (equal number of cells/not cells)

Reminder: only candidate cells will be classified

* highly optimised data loading

## Key take-aways

* `cellfinder` can be used to efficiently find cells in large whole-brain microscopy images
* it uses classical image filtering to find candidates and then classifies them
    * candidates can include many false positives, but _must_ include _all_ true positives
    * usually classification model needs curation and retraining
